newsitem.title: USA: Clinton returns to Washington, key aides to depart.
newsitem.headline: Clinton returns to Washington, key aides to depart.

text.p: A triumphant Bill Clinton returned to the White House on Wednesday to plan a new administration after four Cabinet members, including his secretaries of state and defence, decided to resign.

Flush with his victory over Republican Bob Dole, Clinton flew to Washington from his hometown of Little Rock, Arkansas, where he spent the night after becoming the first Democrat to win re-election to the White House in more than 50 years.
Clinton addressed a "welcome home" rally on the White House South Lawn and was due to attend a victory party in Washington later.

But officials said he had already turned his mind to his next challenge, rearranging his Cabinet, and they said two top aides -- Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry -- had told him they would resign.
One official also said Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor was making plans to return to private life while another reported Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary would leave.
Christopher, 71, and Perry, 69, pillars of Clinton's national security policy, had been widely expected to leave after punishing travel schedules around the world in his first term.
Officials said Christopher, who has flown more than 700,000 miles (1.1 million km) in the president's service since 1992, was expected to keep his post until Clinton's inauguration on January 20.
Separately, they said Perry had told Clinton he planned to resign and may leave the Cabinet to return to private life within a few months, when a successor is chosen.

U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright and former Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell are considered top candidates to succeed Christopher, while there has been speculation that CIA Director John Deutch may take Perry's place.

Officials said Clinton planned to meet with his Cabinet to discuss the changes on Friday. A news conference to unveil the departures, though not necessarily their replacements, was expected to be held soon, possibly on the same day.

Although officials say there is no immediate deadline, several have said Clinton would like to announce some decisions before Tuesday, when he begins a vacation in Hawaii, followed by visits to the Philippines, Australia and Thailand.
Another key appointment -- a replacement for White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta -- is also on the cards, but he has said that he will stay through the transition.

Despite his quick re-immersion in workaday realities, Clinton smiled broadly as he stepped off his Air Force One aircraft, stopping to shake hands exuberantly and pose for photographs with ground staff at Andrews Air Force Base.

Americans sent a mixed message to politicians in Tuesday's election, re-electing Clinton by about 50 percent of the vote to Dole's 41 percent, with 98 percent of ballots counted, while leaving both houses of Congress in Republican hands.

Talking with reporters on Air Force One, Clinton signalled that he wants to reach out to the Republicans, with whom he collaborated on a string of new laws in the final six weeks of the Congressional term.
"If we can somehow recreate for the next four years the spirit that prevailed in the last six weeks of the Congress, we can do great things," Clinton said.
"If we can apply that spirit to balancing the budget, to education reform, to moving people from welfare to work ... we are going to have a great, great opportunity here," he added.
